Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Headache (likely migraine, provisional)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Relief from persistent headaches
  - Avoid disruption to work and daily activities
  - Clarify diagnosis and management options
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Symptom relief with appropriate analgesic therapy
  - Identify triggers and guide on headache management
  - Monitor response to intervention and consider prophylaxis if recurrent
- Actions (Patient):
  - Try prescribed medications (e.g., Naproxen, Paracetamol, Codeine as appropriate)
  - Maintain a headache diary to track frequency, severity, and possible triggers
  - Return for follow-up in 1–2 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Prescribe appropriate analgesics (Naproxen, Paracetamol, Codeine—doses/routes/frequencies not documented)
  - Advise on headache diary and potential need for further investigation or prophylactic therapy if recurrent
  - Provide safety-netting advice (return if worsening, new symptoms, visual changes, limb weakness, or if unwell)
  - Arrange review in 1–2 weeks

Secondary Problem: Work stress
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce impact of headache on ability to work
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Support patient in managing stressors as part of overall headache management
- Actions (Patient):
  - Implement screen brightness adjustment and other ergonomic changes
  - Monitor symptom relationship to work and stress
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Advise regular breaks/screen adjustments at work
  - Consider psychological support/therapy if stress persists (not currently indicated)

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of likely migraine, family history, medication options, when to seek urgent review, keeping a headache diary, possible triggers.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Visual changes, limb weakness, persistent or worsening headaches, inability to function, onset of new symptoms
- Coping Strategies: Medication adherence, environmental adjustments (brightness), rest, monitor for stress triggers, maintain hydration
